extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline, and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural elements used in a USPTO Final Order resolving disciplinary action against a registered patent practitioner, including jurisdictional bases, the substantive misconduct basis, mitigating considerations, agreed sanctions, publication requirements, and waiver provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional authority for proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites the statutory and regulatory bases establishing the Office's authority to approve settlement agreements and issue Final Orders in disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered patent practitioners are bound by the cited federal rules; violations of those rules can give rise to USPTO disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline: public discipline by a State
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) by being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disciplinary action by a state bar or similar authority (public reprimand, etc.) predicates discipline under USPTO rules; the Final Order acknowledges this as the basis for USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive misconduct described in stipulated facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent made false statements in a real estate transaction in which he acted in his personal capacity as a trustee, including falsely telling the seller about an abandoned oil tank, providing a fraudulently produced stock image, misrepresenting ownership to the seller's broker, and giving false statements to a fire department chief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stipulated factual conduct (specific false statements and misrepresentations) serves as the factual basis supporting the disciplinary determination; misconduct may relate to personal, non-client transactions yet still reflect on fitness to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of mitigating factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has acknowledged his ethical lapses, demonstrated genuine contrition, and accepted responsibility for his acts and omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions of wrongdoing, contrition, and acceptance of responsibility are explicit mitigating considerations factored into the agreed sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed sanction: public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent be, and hereby, is publicly reprimanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order imposes a public reprimand as the disciplinary sanction agreed upon by the parties and approved by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room, publicly accessible through the Office's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary Final Orders are to be posted publicly online through the specified USPTO FOIA/OED reading room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided Notice of Public Reprimand wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must identify the respondent, registration number, the violation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), reference the underlying state public reprimand, and state the action is the result of a settlement agreement and the statutory/regulatory provisions invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future use of disciplinary record
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Agreement or the Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding ... (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent ... and (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent (i) as an aggravating factor ... and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly permits the Office to use the record as aggravation or rebuttal in future matters; settlement does not preclude consideration of the conduct again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedural rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, by his agreement, has waived all rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waived the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waived the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement can include explicit waivers of reconsideration, review, and appeal rights; such waivers are incorporated in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement and any Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement specifies that neither party will recover costs from the other as part of the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement submission and approval procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent have submitted a Proposed Settlement Agreement to the Under Secretary of Commerce for Intellectual Property and Director of the USPTO for approval; the agreement resolves all disciplinary action arising from the stipulated facts and is hereby approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary matters may be resolved by stipulated settlement agreements submitted to and approved by the USPTO Director (or delegated authority), resulting in a Final Order that sets forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service / notice to parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order was mailed by email on this day to Respondent via counsel and to the OED Director via email, with counsel contact information listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders include a certificate of service indicating how and to whom the order was provided (counsel for respondent and OED), consistent with procedural requirements for notice.
